A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Connecting Federated ADMM to Bayes. The main text and Appendices A–F are readable, including the equations, Figure 1 and Tables 1–5, and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-learning experiments, including benchmark results in Tables 1–5 and sensitivity and convergence analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised negative log-likelihood results in Table 5.

M1.justification: FedLap, FedLap-Cov and FedLap-Func retain their proposed procedures and update equations. Appendix B corrects the derivation without changing the final implemented update in Eq. 21.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate UCI Credit, FLamby-Heart, MNIST, Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR-10 with the same classification tasks and coverage. No dataset, population or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: FedAvg, FedProx and FedDyn remain the benchmark baselines, and Appendix D retains its FedADMM comparison. Table 4 drops a FedLap-Func column containing only dashes, not evaluated results.

E3.justification: v2 newly describes Table 5 as test negative log-likelihood in Appendix F, while its caption still says validation, as in v1. The PDFs do not establish whether the revised values reflect a changed evaluation split or inconsistent labeling. Other stated splits, model configurations and training budgets match.

E4.justification: Appendix D's weight-decay sensitivity and two-client convergence analyses are retained. The Fashion-MNIST experiment using two shared points per class already appears in v1 Appendix E.5 with identical results; v2 merely adds a main-text pointer.

E5.justification: Run counts, seed disclosures and mean/standard-deviation reporting practices are unchanged. Some standard-deviation values in Table 5 change, but no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 5 revises several Fashion-MNIST entries and all CIFAR-10 entries. At 50 CIFAR-10 rounds, FedDyn/FedLap/FedLap-Cov NLLs change from 1.7/1.3/1.1 to 0.7/0.6/0.6. These are revised reported results, not established same-setting gains given the test/validation ambiguity. Tables 1–4 and Figure 1 retain their results.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the stationary dual variable from the positive to the negative local-loss gradient. Appendix B restores missing one-half factors in the Gaussian KL expression and Eqs. 19–20, making the derivation consistent with the retained precision update.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the ADMM–VB connection through dual and site parameters, covariance and functional-regularisation extensions, and their empirical benefits. The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contribution and novelty scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving uncertainty weighting, functional information and global weight decay, alongside privacy and applicability qualifications, remain substantively unchanged. The new Table 5 discussion repeats interpretations already present in v1's caption.

D1.justification: FedLap-Func documentation replaces explicit first-round input transmission and subsequent prediction-only messaging with an assumption that selected inputs are shared. Several transmission details are consequently omitted. Hyperparameter notation is clarified, while numerical ranges, hardware and runtimes remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The natural-gradient discussion replaces Khan et al. (2018), on Bayesian learning by weight perturbation in Adam, with Khan and Nielsen (2018), on natural-gradient variational inference. This is a limited citation substitution; broader research positioning is retained. The Bayesian Learning Rule reference merely receives publication metadata updates.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording, terminology and notation edits, revises the Section 2 opening, and adds an author-contributions statement. The overall narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 removes its empty FedLap-Func column, and captions, spacing and page breaks receive small adjustments. Figure 1 preserves its plotted curves, uncertainty bands, axes and legend; the five-table presentation remains otherwise similar.

improvement.justification: The sign and coefficient corrections in Section 2 and Appendix B improve mathematical consistency with the stated updates, providing a concrete but localized reliability gain. The methods and main empirical evidence remain stable. This gain is tempered by unexplained Table 5 revisions, its new test/validation inconsistency, and less explicit initial data-sharing details.
